reason: Attacked and survived, and the attack removed the one real weakness in the verdict, which was that the shipped punctuation rested on a composite of two reprints plus an unnamed web transcription. The verifier's own evidence concedes it: the 1907 Universal Library scan keeps the dash and loses the comma at the line break reli-gion, the 1906 scan keeps the comma and loses every dash. Building a reading out of two witnesses neither of which carries it is close to minting, so I went for a single witness. I downloaded the 1907 scan the evidence links, normalised its whitespace and found the passage at page 287 under the running head CHAP. XVI OF MODERN LANDSCAPE, and it reads religion followed by a dash and no comma, exactly as the evidence admits. I then searched the Internet Archive for the 1856 printing, downloaded modernpainters0003unse_q9h7 and found the passage there under the running head OF MODERN LANDSCAPE, page 268, PART IV, at section 28. It reads: Then, as touching the kind of work done by these two men, the more I think of it I find this conclusion more impressed upon me, then a dash, that the greatest thing a human soul ever does in this world is to see something, and tell what it saw in a plain way. Hundreds of people can talk for one who can think, but thousands can think for one who can see. To see clearly is poetry, prophecy, and religion, then a comma, then a dash, then all in one. So the exact punctuation on the card, comma then dash, is in one printing of the named edition, with no compositing needed, and Ruskin's comma-dash is his own habit and appears twice in that one sentence group. The same file settles the rest of the source line: its table of contents heads PART IV. OF MANY THINGS, the chapter is CHAPTER XVI. OF MODERN LANDSCAPE, the section mark is section 28, and the preface is dated Denmark Hill, Jan. 1856, so Volume III, Part IV, ch. XVI, Of Modern Landscape, section 28, 1856 is right in every element and the page in that printing is 268, not the 287 of the 1907 reprint. The quotation begins at a sentence boundary and ends at one, and the sentence dropped before it, about the greatest thing a human soul ever does, is the sentence that sets it up, so nothing is distorted by starting where the card starts. Attribution is Ruskin's own prose, not reported and not a character's, so no speaker is owed, and nothing on the misattribution list touches it. shipped.js: john ruskin, no shipped hit, no near hit, zero of three for the year, not banned. Source line leads with the name, carries no dash, no straight double quote, 98 characters. Tag Essay is the only fit in the closed vocabulary for critical prose and matches the precedent the track already set for Stevenson's travel prose in carry-in 02-cfl-03. Scope is clean, 1856, publishable, and on theme it is the month's own thesis stated by the man who spent his life on it. I could not break it.

residual: The quotation carries an em dash. Rule five bans the em dash in the source and in the note and says nothing about the quotation, and a quotation keeps its edition's punctuation, so it may stand. But if any later pass strips dashes from card text, this line changes wording: religion, all in one with the comma alone appears in no printing I read, and religion all in one with the dash alone is the 1907 reprint's reading, not the 1856 one. Flagged so it is a decision and not an accident. The verifier's evidence also quotes page 287, which is the 1907 reprint's pagination, while the source line dates the edition 1856, where the page is 268; nothing on the card says a page, so this is a note for the register rather than a fault.
